title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: PAC recurring audit lapses
sections.summary: The PAC is concerned that many audit issues in the Auditor-General's report were recurring, prompting Permanent Secretaries from four Ministries to explain the lapses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While we do not expect zero gaps and weaknesses for a government machinery of this scale and complexity, what concerns the PAC Members is that many of the audit issues brought up in the Auditor-General's report were recurring items that happen year after year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Some of the lapses this year concerned the PAC Members so much that Permanent Secretaries from four Ministries were also asked to meet the Committee to explain the reasons for the lapses and what are the detailed follow-up measures taken to address the lapses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The PAC was concerned that given the increasing size and complexity of the work in the public sector, such lapses, if not addressed fundamentally, may compound over time and weaken the governance and accountability over the judicious use of public funds and resources.

sections.label: Budget funds for protection
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister highlighted plans to set aside $5 billion for the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund and $1 billion for cyber and data security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the Budget, the Deputy Prime Minister highlighted plans to set aside funds for an initial injection of $5 billion for the new Coastal and Flood Protection Fund, $1 billion for building up the Government’s cyber and data security capabilities and there are also further plans to build new housing estates, increase the green cover in the residential estates and so on.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme funding
sections.summary: The Government has invested substantial funds to support firms to transform and grow under the Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government has invested substantial funds to support firms to transform and grow under the Industry Transformation Programme (ITMs).

sections.label: Temasek succession planning question
sections.summary: In 2017, the speaker asked a Parliamentary Question about succession planning in Temasek Holdings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, in 2017, I asked a Parliamentary Question about succession planning in Temasek Holdings.

sections.label: CEO succession and remuneration disclosure
sections.summary: The public has a legitimate interest in why CEO succession saw no concrete movement in 11 years and whether top executive remuneration is consistent with market norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The public has a legitimate interest in understanding, for instance, why Chief Executive Officer (CEO) succession was deemed to be enough of a priority in 2009 to appoint a CEO-designate, and yet, there has not been any concrete movement or succession on the 11 years since then, in spite of what one must assume would be no lack of suitable candidates internally or externally, or whether remuneration given to top executives is consistent with market norms and represents good value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In contrast, the Singapore code of corporate governance calls on listed companies to disclose total remuneration paid to the top five key management personnel.

sections.label: Bipartisan committee for SWFs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would allow a bipartisan Parliamentary Committee to interview key personnel from SWFs yearly for accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider, at the very least, allowing a bipartisan Parliamentary Committee to interview the key personnel from these SWFs once a year so that there is some degree of accountability to legislators?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: According to McKinsey, applying AI to nine business functions in 19 industries has the potential to create between US$3.5 trillion and US$5.8 trillion in value annually.

sections.label: Parenthood tax rebates for unmarried parents
sections.summary: A question asks why unmarried parents do not receive parenthood tax rebates like other parents.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng, you can do both your cuts together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They are no less a mother or a father just because their child was born outside of marriage." Why do they not then get the parenthood tax rebates like other parents?

sections.label: Working Mother's Child Relief for single unweds
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOF will let single unweds qualify for the Working Mother's Child Relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOF consider allowing single unweds to qualify for the Working Mother's Child Relief?

sections.label: Foreign Maid Levy Relief for single fathers
sections.summary: The taxman does not treat a male taxpayer the same as the opposite gender for Foreign Maid Levy Relief claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: While the role and responsibility of being a single parent are not any lesser for a single father, the taxman does not treat a male taxpayer in the same light as the opposite gender when it comes to claiming for Foreign Maid Levy (FML) Relief.

sections.label: Gender-neutral Foreign Maid Levy Relief
sections.summary: The Foreign Maid Levy Relief has to be gender-neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Foreign Maid Levy Relief has to be gender-neutral.

sections.label: Government procurement for SMEs and startups
sections.summary: A question asks how MOF can enhance Government procurement to help SMEs and startups develop innovative solutions and grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MOF share how we can enhance the Government procurement approach to enable SMEs and startups to develop innovative solutions and, in doing so, also help them to grow?

sections.label: MOF digitalisation of service delivery
sections.summary: A question asks how MOF has tapped on digitalisation to enhance service delivery and interactions with businesses and citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: How has MOF tapped on digitalisation to enhance its service delivery and interactions with businesses and citizens?

sections.label: MOF partnerships with citizens
sections.summary: Asks how MOF has increased partnership and co-creation with citizens, businesses and the community under the Singapore Together movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: As part of the Singapore Together movement, how has MOF increased partnership and co-creation with citizens, businesses and the community in delivering solutions?

sections.label: Ministry community business partnerships
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry can enable more partnerships with community and businesses to co-create solutions and build a caring society.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Under the Singapore Together movement, how can the Ministry enable more partnerships with the community and businesses to co-create, deliver solutions and build a more caring and resilient society?

sections.label: Insurance discrimination special needs
sections.summary: States that people with special needs face insurance discrimination for declaration of their medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Today, people with special needs face insurance discrimination for declaration of their medical conditions.

sections.label: MediShield Life CareShield Life coverage
sections.summary: States MediShield Life and soon-to-be-introduced CareShield Life will help, but may not apply for all depending on conditions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: MediShield Life and soon-to-be-introduced CareShield Life will help, but they may not apply for all, depending on conditions.

sections.label: COVID-19 fiscal sustainability reminder
sections.summary: States the COVID-19 outbreak and its economic fallout remind why ensuring long-term fiscal sustainability is critical.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 virus outbreak and its economic fallout are a timely reminder of why it is critical to ensure long-term fiscal sustainability.

sections.label: Productivity growth rise
sections.summary: States overall productivity growth rose to 2.6% per year in the last three years, up from 2.2%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the last three years, overall productivity growth, as measured by real value-added per actual hour worked, rose to 2.6% per year, up from the 2.2% per year in the preceding three-year period.

sections.label: RIE investments and R&D spending
sections.summary: RIE investments supported over 5,500 industry jobs, and business R&D expenditure rose from $4.5 billion in 2011 to $5.6 billion in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As at end March 2019, our RIE investments have supported the creation of more than 5,500 industry jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Business expenditure in R&D has grown steadily since the start of RIE2015, from $4.5 billion in 2011 to $5.6 billion in 2018, or an increase of about 25%.

sections.label: Reduced block Budget spending growth
sections.summary: In 2017 and 2018, the spending cap and annual growth rate of block Budgets were reduced to manage expenditure growth.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In 2017 and 2018, we reduced both the spending cap and the annual growth rate of the block Budgets, to further manage expenditure growth.

sections.label: Savings from infrastructure project reviews
sections.summary: Over five years, these processes led to design improvements and about $3.5 billion in savings for infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, these processes have led to design improvements and generated savings of about $3.5 billion for infrastructure projects.

sections.label: ICT project cost savings and panel
sections.summary: ICT project reviews achieved about 6% or $900 million in savings over five years, and an ICT advisory panel of industry experts will be formed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Similarly, through the review processes for ICT projects, we have been able to achieve cost savings of about 6%, or $900 million, over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To further strengthen our scrutiny over ICT spending, we will be inviting industry experts to form an ICT advisory panel to benefit from their private sector perspectives in the evaluation of major Government ICT projects.

sections.label: LTA street lighting award savings
sections.summary: The Smart and Energy-Efficient Street Lighting System won the MOT VFM Distinguished Award and led to about $4 million in yearly cost savings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: One LTA project that recently won the MOT VFM Distinguished Award is the Smart and Energy-Efficient Street Lighting System which provides higher energy efficiency, as well as reduced manpower and time to detect and rectify defects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This led to cost savings of about $4 million every year.

sections.label: KidSTART expansion to more children
sections.summary: Based on preliminary results and positive feedback, the Government and MOF will expand KidSTART to benefit another 5,000 children over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Based on the preliminary results and positive feedback, the Government and MOF had the confidence to expand KidSTART to benefit another 5,000 children over the next three years.

sections.label: GIC and Temasek mandate
sections.summary: GIC and Temasek are commercially-run entities with arm's-length government ties, whose boards handle operations and succession, focused on long-term financial returns for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Both GIC and Temasek are commercially-run entities, and the Government maintains an arm's-length relationship with them.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The boards of these entities are ultimately responsible for their respective operations, performances as well as succession for leadership.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For these two entities, the focus and the mandate that we have put on them are to generate long-term financial returns for the benefit of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Government benefits for children
sections.summary: Government benefits supporting children's growth are extended regardless of parents' marital status, while Parenthood Tax Rebate and Working Mother's Child Relief support parenthood within marriage.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Where there are Government benefits that support the child's growth and development, we will extend them, regardless of their parents' marital status.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why all Singaporean children today receive over $180,000 of education subsidies by the time they turn 16, at least $6,000 in their Child Development Account (CDA) Grants and $4,000 in MediSave Grant for Newborns.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For the Parenthood Tax Rebate and Working Mother's Child Relief, these were intended to support parenthood within marriage and for married mothers to continue working after childbirth.

sections.label: Cost-effective ICT contract solution
sections.summary: This approach secured a more cost-effective solution for a large ICT contract, tens of millions of dollars lower than the original bid price.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For instance, through this approach, we were able to secure a more cost-effective solution for a large ICT contract at tens of millions of dollars lower than the original bid price.

sections.label: Dynamic contracts for ICT tenders
sections.summary: Agencies gain faster access to newer technology, saving about three months each time; dynamic contracts piloted for two ICT bulk tenders over $700 million will scale to three more.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Agencies can have faster access to newer technology and capabilities, leading to time savings of about three months each time this feature is used.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have piloted the use of dynamic contracts for two ICT bulk tenders amounting to more than $700 million and will scale this up to three more bulk tenders this year.

sections.label: Automated audit controls and monitoring
sections.summary: Automating audit controls and background monitoring will save public officers more than 100,000 mandays a year, freeing time to deliver better public services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Audit controls will be automated and monitoring done in the background.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This will save our public officers more than 100,000 mandays a year, freeing up their time to focus on delivering better services to the public.

sections.label: Procurement awards to SMEs and startups
sections.summary: More than 80% of the total number of procurement opportunities are awarded to SMEs and startups.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: More than 80% of the total number of procurement opportunities are awarded to SMEs and startups.

sections.label: Open Innovation Platform challenges
sections.summary: Since July 2018, agencies have posted 13 challenges on OIP with prize monies over half a million dollars.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since its launch in July 2018, agencies have posted 13 challenges on OIP to invite the public to submit solutions, with prize monies of more than half a million dollars.

sections.label: Electronic signature option by 2023
sections.summary: Under the Digital Government Blueprint, all Government interactions with businesses and citizens will include an electronic signature option by 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As part of the Digital Government Blueprint, all Government interactions with businesses and citizens will include an electronic signature option by 2023.

sections.label: 200,000 companies may benefit
sections.summary: With the launch later this year, about 200,000 companies can potentially benefit from this initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With the launch later this year, about 200,000 companies can potentially benefit from this initiative.

sections.label: Tax filing pilot and chatbot
sections.summary: A form piloted with over 600 drivers was more intuitive and cut filing time 30%, so IRAS and GovTech are prototyping a chatbot for about 6,000 drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The form was piloted last year with over 600 drivers who found this tax filing process more intuitive.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: They also spent 30% less time filing their returns.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Given its success, IRAS is working with GovTech on a prototype chatbot to benefit about 6,000 taxi and PHC drivers during this year's tax filing season.

sections.label: Scheme benefited 10,000 SMEs
sections.summary: With their support, the scheme has benefited over 10,000 SMEs since its launch in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With their support, the scheme has benefited over 10,000 SMEs since its launch in 2019.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan work groups
sections.summary: MSF formed three Enabling Masterplan work groups, and the passage states children born outside marriage do not qualify for the Parenthood Tax Rebate and Working Mother's Child Relief.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) has formed three Enabling Masterplan work groups to guide us in building a more inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, our work is not done in creating a better Singapore for all.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We encourage our businesses, community groups and individuals to come forward and work together with us to build and sustain Singapore's success for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It does not really matter whether the child was born out of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But here we are now saying that they are not equal, that because the child was born outside of marriage, they will not qualify for the Parenthood Tax Rebate and the Working Mother's Child Relief.

sections.label: Parenthood tax rebate deterrence doubt
sections.summary: The speaker doubts the Parenthood Tax Rebate and Working Mother's Child Relief deter, and says single unweds' median income under 35 is $600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But again, as I raised in my Adjournment Motion, I doubt this will be a deterrence, unless, just before they have sex, they think about the Parenthood Tax Rebate and Working Mother's Child Relief, which we know, will not happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I am not really fighting for a lot of money here and I do not think actually a lot of single unweds pay a lot of taxes, because we know their median income is $600 for those under 35.

sections.label: Support creates marriage gradient
sections.summary: Members asked for such support, but providing it would create a gradient between parenthood incentives within and outside marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Various Members of the House have asked for such support, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And if you were to provide that support, there will invariably be a gradient between incentives and encouragement for parenthood within the context of marriage versus outside of marriage.

sections.label: NIRC long-term revenue source
sections.summary: NIRC will be an important source of revenue over the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, NIRC will be an important source of revenue over the long term.

sections.label: Long-term returns pressure
sections.summary: Long-term trends mean continued pressures on Singapore's long-term expected returns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If we think about these long-term trends, then indeed, there will be continued pressures on our long-term expected returns.

sections.label: NIRC growth versus rate of return
sections.summary: NIRC growth does not equal the long-term expected rate of return, since NIRC is base multiplied by rate of return, evaluated yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, there are two figures which we should not conflate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: One is the growth of NIRC but that does not equate to the long-term expected rate of return, because NIRC is the base multiplied by the rate of return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As far as the rate of return is concerned, this is evaluated every year.

sections.label: Geopolitical tensions and deglobalisation returns
sections.summary: Continued geopolitical tensions and growing deglobalisation may impact expected returns over the longer term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It need not impact on the immediate long-term expected rate of return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we are concerned indeed that over a period of time, if these trends were to continue, if you see continued geopolitical tensions, if you see a growing trend of deglobalisation, then indeed, expected returns over the longer term may be impacted.

sections.label: NIRC long-term expected returns
sections.summary: The NIRC uses long-term expected returns of investment entities, so negative market performance in a year does not impact it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the first part, the NIRC or the long-term expected return is looking at long-term what the investment entities are expecting in terms of their returns over a long period of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, if this year's market performance ends up negative, stock markets everywhere were to crash and overall returns are negative, it does not impact on our NIRC.

sections.label: Debt financing for infrastructure
sections.summary: The debt financing arrangement is still being worked out, with the idea of borrowing for selected major infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the second part, we are still working out the debt financing arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The idea is that we will borrow for selected major infrastructure.
